summary: Mars's seven-year mahadasha is a period of energy, effort and conflict: income through land, courage, authority, fighting, medicine or fire, alongside quarrels with siblings and family and illness from heat, bile and blood. BPHS makes it strongly favourable (high position, land, wealth, victory over enemies) when Mars is exalted, in its own or moolatrikona sign, or strong in a kendra, the 2nd, 3rd or 11th, and troubled when Mars is debilitated, in the 6th, 8th or 12th, or afflicted by malefics.
common_outcomes: money made through land, litigation and dealings with rulers; more land and cattle (Phaladeepika 19.20)
wealth through fire, rulers, fighting and the like, and also through medicine, deceit and harsh dealings (Phaladeepika 19.9; Jataka Parijata 18.84)
quarrels with brothers, sons, wife, relatives and elders (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20; Jataka Parijata 18.84)
illness from bile, blood, fever and heat (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20; Jataka Parijata 18.84)
when well placed: land, fulfilled wishes, clarity of mind, courage, money, defeat of enemies, support of younger siblings (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI, p. 144-145)
when strong: high position, recognition from government, wealth and land, gains from abroad, vehicles and ornaments, harmony with siblings (BPHS 47.27-30)
rare_outcomes: rise to a kingdom or command at the head of a large army, when exalted Mars is in the 10th or 11th or in an upward-facing sign (Phaladeepika 20.25)
loss of eyesight or injury to the eye, cuts from weapons, when Mars is unfavourable (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI, p. 145)
mortgaging of landed property and loss of spouse and children for Mars in Libra (Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, p. 245)
having to eat poor, unwholesome food (Jataka Parijata 18.84)

by_area.personality: Courage, effort and clarity of mind when Mars is favourable (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); a harsher, scheming streak and envy of others' fortune when it is not (Phaladeepika 19.9).
by_area.career: High administrative or political position and government recognition when Mars is strong (BPHS 47.27-30); income through rulers, fighting, the military, medicine or fire (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20); military success and respect for skill for Mars in Capricorn (Raman). Trouble with rulers and superiors when Mars is afflicted (Uttara Kalamrita; Raman for Cancer and Aquarius).
by_area.finance: Wealth through valour, land and property, gains from abroad (BPHS 47.27-31); money through land and litigation, but also loss of wealth (Phaladeepika 19.20); loss of wealth and distress when Mars is debilitated or in a dusthana (BPHS 47.33).
by_area.health: Fevers and illness from bile, blood and heat (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20; Jataka Parijata 18.84); wounds, cuts from weapons and eye trouble when Mars is unfavourable (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from spouse and children when Mars is strong in a kendra or the 3rd (BPHS 47.31-32); quarrels with wife and children and liaisons with low company otherwise (Phaladeepika 19.9; Jataka Parijata 18.84).
by_area.family: Siblings are central: happiness and good relations with co-borns when Mars is strong (BPHS 47.30; Uttara Kalamrita), quarrels with brothers and relatives when it is not (Phaladeepika 19.20; Raman for Cancer, Libra).

strengtheners: Mars exalted, in its moolatrikona or own sign (BPHS 47.27-30)
Mars strong in a kendra, the 11th or the 2nd, in a benefic navamsa, joined or aspected by benefics (BPHS 47.27-30)
Mars strong in a kendra or the 3rd: wealth through valour and victory (BPHS 47.31)
Mars as yogakaraka for Cancer and Leo lagnas, and as 2nd and 9th lord for Pisces lagna (Santhanam's note to BPHS 47.33; Laghu Parashari v. 12)
Mars exalted in the 10th or 11th, or in an upward-facing sign (Phaladeepika 20.25)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars debilitated, in the 6th, 8th or 12th, or joined or aspected by malefics (BPHS 47.33)
a malefic in depression, an enemy sign, the 6th or the 12th gives intense misery in its dasha (Phaladeepika 20.27)
Mars combust (BPHS 47.6, general rule as read in the Sanskrit gloss; Phaladeepika 20.22: mixed results)
Mars's dasha falling fifth in the sequence from birth is called dangerous (Phaladeepika 20.24)
Mars in Cancer, Libra or Aquarius (Raman, ch. XXIV)
lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role matters as much as sign: Santhanam (note to BPHS 47.33) says Mars, ruling a kendra and a trikona, is yogakaraka for Cancer (5th and 10th) and Leo (4th and 9th) lagnas, and as 2nd and 9th lord is very good for Pisces lagna, so its dasha is very beneficial there if Mars is unafflicted. Laghu Parashari (v. 12, tr. O.P. Verma) adds that a malefic like Mars becomes auspicious by kendra lordship only when it also rules a trikona; for Aquarius lagna (3rd and 10th lord) it is called evil. Frawley (p. 245) lists Mars as generally benefic for Cancer, Leo, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas and usually good for Aries and Scorpio. Uttara Kalamrita (p. 251) says that in Mars's mahadasha Saturn's sub-period gives Mars's own results and vice versa. No source read gives Mars-dasha results by house counted from the Moon.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.27-33, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 580-581
source_views.view: Exalted, moolatrikona or own-sign Mars, or Mars strong in a kendra, the 11th or 2nd, in a benefic navamsa and with a benefic: high position, wealth and land, government recognition, gains from abroad, vehicles, ornaments, happiness with siblings. Strong in a kendra or the 3rd: wealth through valour, victory over enemies, happiness from spouse and children, but some unfavourable effects at the end of the dasha. Debilitated, in the 6th, 8th or 12th, or with or aspected by malefics: loss of wealth and distress. Santhanam's note: yogakaraka for Cancer and Leo, very good for Pisces lagna, if unafflicted.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3-6 and 47.27-33, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: The gloss adds trikona to the favourable houses (v. 28), reads the benefic as aspecting (v. 29), and gives happiness at the start of the dasha and trouble at its end (v. 32). Verses 3-4 time results by the planet's decanate (first decanate early, second middle, third late; reversed when retrograde); verses 5-6 make a dasha good if its lord is in the lagna, exalted, own or friendly sign, and bad if in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign.

19.9: wealth through fire, rulers and fighting, and also by medicine, falsehood and cruel acts; constant bile, blood and fever trouble; low company; quarrels with wife, children, relatives and elders; enjoying others' fortune. 19.20: money through land, litigation and the ruler; more cattle and land; quarrels with brothers and sons; wicked company; diseases of bile, blood and fire; loss of wealth.

20.25: Mars in an upward-facing sign, or exalted in the 10th or 11th, gives a kingdom, victory over enemies, vehicles and an army. 20.24: the fifth dasha from birth belonging to Mars is dangerous. 20.22: a vargottama dasha lord gives good results, an eclipsed or debilitated one mixed results. 20.27: malefics in depression, enemy signs, 6th or 12th give intense misery. 20.40: powerful lords of or planets in the 2nd and 7th can cause death in their dashas. 20.57: a debilitated or combust planet in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives mixed results, good in the latter half.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.84 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II p. 1042)
source_views.view: Money through arms, wars between kings and other means, also through medicine, trickery, fraud and cruel acts; fever from bile and blood; low company; hatred from sons, wife, relatives and elders, and as a result poor food. Nearly identical to Phaladeepika 19.9.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI (tr. P.S. Sastri, pp. 144-145, 251)
source_views.view: Highly beneficial Mars: land, desired objects, wisdom, clarity, valour, money, defeat of enemies, younger siblings. Unfavourable Mars: distress to younger siblings, quarrels, trouble over land and fire, wounds, eye trouble, trouble from government, anger of the learned, weapon cuts, disease. Page 251: in Mars's mahadasha Saturn's sub-period gives Mars's results, and Mars's results come in Saturn's sub-period.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari v. 12 (tr. O.P. Verma, pp. 47-48)
source_views.view: Mars does not become auspicious merely by owning the 10th; only with a trikona lordship as well (Cancer lagna, 5th and 10th) is it a yogakaraka. For Aquarius lagna (3rd and 10th) it is evil.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 244-245
source_views.view: Results by Mars's sign. Good: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Pisces (wealth, fame, success, land, victory, learning). Bad: Cancer (enemies, litigation, ill health, family discord), Libra (misery, family losses, mortgaged property), Aquarius (hardship, friction with superiors, trouble to mother and servants). He also warns that results vary with the dasha lord's strength, aspects and navamsa.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, pp. 202-203, 245-247
source_views.view: General: the major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects; the start of a period is the time to balance it with gems, mantras or worship. For Mars: benefic for Cancer, Leo, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas; red coral (avoid if Mars is a malefic lord, esp. Gemini and Virgo lagna, or in the 7th); mantras OM KUJAYA NAMAHA, OM KUM, OM ANGARAKAYA NAMAHA; deity Skanda. His dasha chapter gives no Mars-specific period results.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach ch. 16.5
source_views.view: General only: a planet gives in its dasha what its positions in the divisional charts promise; judge the mahadasha mainly from the Sun, antardashas from the Moon, with the dasha lord as a further reference. No Mars-specific results.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 21-22, 162
source_views.view: Examples only: for P.V. Narasimha Rao, Mars as 3rd and 8th lord with the 12th lord Sun in the 10th (a vipareeta raja yoga) brought him to Prime Minister in Mars dasha; another native's Mars dasha took him away from home to finish his education.

disagreements: Phaladeepika and Jataka Parijata describe the dasha mostly in mixed or harsh terms (gains through land and fighting, but quarrels and bile/blood illness), while BPHS makes it strongly good or bad depending on dignity and house. Santhanam's BPHS 47.32 says the strong-Mars dasha has some unfavourable effects at its end; the Sanskrit gloss reads it as happiness at the start and trouble at the end. Santhanam lists the favourable houses as kendra, 11th and 2nd; the gloss adds trikona. Raman makes Cancer (debilitation) and also Libra and Aquarius bad signs, but Santhanam's note makes Mars a yogakaraka for Cancer lagna, so sign and functional role can pull in opposite directions.
phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a high-energy, effort-driven period: good for property, initiative, competition and courage, with a need to manage temper, disputes (especially with siblings and family) and heat-related health. Stress the favourable version only when the chart shows a strong or yogakaraka Mars. Do not predict deaths, accidents or surgery; at most suggest care with health, safety and conflict.

phases: BPHS 47.32: when Mars is strong in a kendra or the 3rd, some unfavourable effects come at the end of the dasha (the Sanskrit gloss: happiness at the start, trouble at the end). BPHS 47.3-4: a planet in the first decanate of its sign gives its results at the start of the dasha, the second in the middle, the third at the end; the order reverses if the planet is retrograde. Phaladeepika 20.57: a weak Mars in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives its good results in the latter half.
